findings.summary: Pure queued-shell run: jobs.json shows total_count=0 — the run sat queued from 18:00:59Z and was cancelled at 18:01:13Z without any job starting, so ZERO agent tokens/compute were spent and no council work existed to lose. The substantive artifact of this moment is the triggering commit itself (d7f67fe, durable on main), not any run output.

Cancellation cause is PLAUSIBLY attributed but not provable locally: sibling council run #10 (32881307714) was created 18:01:12Z, one second before this run's cancellation timestamp — matching the empirically adjudicated newest-queued-run-wins semantics inside group spider-critical-cto-council documented for council #6/#7 (runs 32879459085/32879902647) even under cancel-in-progress=false. Logs are 0 bytes because no job ever started, so no shutdown/cancel signature can ever be recovered from them; definitive confirmation would require the live API's cancellation actor fields.

Fetch-harness fingerprint lesson: bundle reports log_status='available' with a 0-byte logs.txt while jobs.json proves total_count=0. For zero-job queued-cancelled runs an EMPTY log is the expected legitimate outcome, so log_status alone cannot distinguish 'no job ever ran' from 'fetch failed'; the jobs array is the discriminating field. Mirrors (inverted) the caveat first recorded for run 32894986672.

failure_signatures: None in-run (no job started). Batch-level signature: created→cancelled ≈14s with jobs=[] during the 18:00:56–18:06:32Z control-plane iteration burst (six commits d7f67fe→b4dbd70, each re-triggering council/curator/hygiene workflows).
